10.1002_adfm.78948: Introducing multidentate organic passivators has emerged as an effective strategy for defect passivation at the buried interface of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the active polar functional groups within these passivators are prone to supramolecular polymerization, which compromises passivation effectiveness. Herein, a supramolecular depolymerization strategy synergistically driven by thermal annealing and heteromolecular interactions is proposed. This approach enables the in situ depolymerization of the Zaltoprofen (Za) supramolecular structures introduced at the buried interface. The resulting depolymerized Za molecules are effectively anchored onto the underlying hole transport layer (HTL), while their molecular orientation is optimized to expose Lewis base coordination sites toward the perovskite layer. Consequently, enhanced coordination interactions with undercoordinated Pb 2+ are achieved, leading to more effective interfacial defect passivation and improved charge extraction. As a result, inverted PSCs based on a 1.57 eV bandgap perovskite exhibit a significantly improved power conversion efficiency ( PCE ), increasing from 24.05% to 25.61%. Moreover, the devices treated with this strategy demonstrate substantially enhanced operational stability compared with the pristine devices. This work provides a simple and effective strategy for activating supramolecular passivators and maximizing their defect‐passivation capability in high‐efficiency inverted PSCs.
10.1002_adma.73676: The initial irreversible capacity loss (ICL) during the first charge significantly reduces the energy and power densities of lithium‑ion batteries (LIBs). Conventional prelithiation additives suffer from limited theoretical specific capacities (300–1000 mAh g −1 ), poor air stability, and low conversion efficiency. Herein, K 3 P 7 , which possesses high solubility in ester‐based electrolytes, is introduced as an electrolyte additive to improve the reversible capacities of various commercial LIBs. It provides an exceptional capacity‑compensation effect through the oxidation of P 7 3− , equivalent to 3048 mAh g −1 . Additionally, K + ions intercalate into the graphite interlayer, expanding the interlayer spacing and thereby improving the high‑rate performance of the graphite anode. The additive also promotes the formation of a stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and a uniform solid electrolyte interface (SEI), contributing to improved cycle stability of both electrodes. Furthermore, K 3 P 7 effectively scavenges free radicals, alleviating gas generation and internal pressure build‑up. When applied in a LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||graphite full cell, the initial reversible capacity is 8% higher than that of the control sample, and the cell retains 92.9% of its capacity after 200 cycles. This work reveals a facile multi‐functional electrolyte additive that enhances the overall performance of LIBs.
10.1002_aenm.71281: Practical application of high‐load iodine cathodes in zinc‐iodine batteries encounters challenges related to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish iodine redox kinetics. Overcoming these issues requires the development of advanced host materials capable of trapping polyiodides and enhancing Zn‐I 2 redox reactions. In this regard, we incorporated ultrafine silver nanoparticles into a N‐doped mesoporous carbon fiber framework (Ag@CMFs), thereby constructing an integrated tandem‐structured host that leverages an “Integrated Spatial Confinement‐Chemical Anchoring‐Conductive Network” synergistic effect to accelerate the catalytic conversion and adsorption of polyiodides. The host effectively immobilizes all iodine species (I 2 /I − /I 3 − /I 5 − ) on the electrode surface. Benefiting from the synergistic merits of the host, the Ag@CMFs/I 2 cathode (high iodine loading: 14.72 mg cm −2 ) delivers reversible capacities of 208.1 mAh g −1 at 1 C and 180.6 mAh g −1 at 10 C, with Coulombic efficiency maintained above 99.5%. Furthermore, exceptional cycling stability is demonstrated with an impressive capacity retention rate of 80.7% after 92 000 cycles at 50 C. The pouch cell delivers an areal capacity of 6.5 mAh cm −2 and remains stable for over 300 cycles with an ultrahigh iodine loading of 3200 mg. This study offers fresh perspectives on host architecture to prevent polyiodide shuttle behaviour and guarantee long‐lasting cycle stability of Zn–I 2 batteries.
10.1002_anie.202520105: Layered oxide cathodes are primary candidates for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries, which often suffer from structural degradation during deep Na + (de)intercalation processes. Incorporating electrochemically inactive cations into the transition metal (TM) layers has emerged as a mainstream strategy to enhance structural stability through the so‐called pinning effect. However, the microstructural heterogeneity of inactive cations within the TM layers and the spatial extent of their influence remain poorly understood. In this work, we regulate the pinning domain by modulating configurational entropy of inactive ions (S config ‐I), thereby promoting their dispersion and maximizing the spatial extent of the pinning effect. Additionally, we establish a correlation between S config ‐I and local structural fluctuations using quantitative experimental analyses. Compared with samples lacking sufficient pinning domains, the sample with 21% S config ‐I (denoted as S‐I‐21%) exhibits markedly improved structural homogeneity and optimally dispersed pinning dopants. Accordingly, S‐I‐21% delivers a high reversible capacity of 145 mAh g −1 and maintains ∼80% capacity retention after 500 cycles within a wide voltage window (2.0−4.3 V). These findings highlight the effect domain of dopants and their role in regulating structural chemistry, providing design principles for robust layered cathodes.
